hypotheses.title: J147 Lifespan Extension Requires Neuronal AMPK
hypotheses.claim: J147 extends lifespan in Drosophila melanogaster lacking neuronal AMPK. The compound will increase longevity in flies without neuronal AMPK under standard laboratory conditions.
hypotheses.rationale: J147 may act through AMPK-independent neuroprotective mechanisms such as reduced oxidative damage and improved mitochondrial function. These pathways can operate in neurons even when AMPK signaling is absent.
hypotheses.prediction: Supplemented flies lacking neuronal AMPK will show significantly longer median and maximum lifespan than untreated controls.
hypotheses.experiment: Raise AMPK-null neuronal Drosophila melanogaster cohorts with and without J147 in their food and measure age-specific survival to death under identical conditions.

hypotheses.title: J147 Extends Lifespan in Drosophila melanogaster
hypotheses.claim: J147 extends lifespan in Drosophila melanogaster. Flies receiving the compound in their diet will live longer than flies receiving vehicle alone.
hypotheses.rationale: J147 is a small molecule with broad neuroprotective and metabolic effects, and interventions that improve cellular stress resistance commonly slow aging in flies.
hypotheses.prediction: J147-treated flies will show significantly increased median and maximum lifespan compared with vehicle-treated controls.
hypotheses.experiment: Maintain matched Drosophila melanogaster cohorts on food with and without J147 and measure age-specific survival to death under identical conditions.

hypotheses.experiment: Maintain matched Drosophila melanogaster cohorts on food with and without octoclothepin or loxapine and measure age-specific survival to death under identical conditions.

hypotheses.experiment: Maintain matched Drosophila melanogaster cohorts on food with and without cardamonin and measure age-specific survival to death under identical conditions.

hypotheses.title: Cardamonin Shortens Lifespan in Drosophila melanogaster
hypotheses.claim: Cardamonin shortens lifespan in Drosophila melanogaster. Flies receiving cardamonin in their diet will live shorter than flies receiving vehicle alone.
hypotheses.rationale: Cardamonin can be cytotoxic at sufficient concentrations and may disrupt endogenous signaling or detoxification, and compounds imposing such stress commonly accelerate aging in flies.
hypotheses.prediction: Cardamonin-treated flies will show significantly decreased median and maximum lifespan compared with vehicle-treated controls.
hypotheses.experiment: Maintain matched Drosophila melanogaster cohorts on food with and without cardamonin and measure age-specific survival to death under identical conditions.

hypotheses.title: Cardamonin Extends Lifespan via Nrf2 Activation
hypotheses.claim: Cardamonin extends lifespan in Drosophila melanogaster by activating the Nrf2 oxidative stress response pathway. Flies receiving cardamonin will live longer through Nrf2-dependent enhancement of antioxidant defenses.
hypotheses.rationale: Nrf2 signaling upregulates antioxidant and detoxification genes, and cardamonin is known to activate this pathway, providing a mechanistic route to reduced oxidative damage and slower aging.
hypotheses.prediction: Cardamonin will extend lifespan in control flies but not in flies with impaired Nrf2 signaling, and Nrf2 target genes will be induced by treatment.
hypotheses.experiment: Maintain matched Drosophila melanogaster cohorts with intact and genetically impaired Nrf2 signaling on food with and without cardamonin and measure age-specific survival to death under identical conditions.
